What each node needs#

All thirty-one node types are in the palette, and most work on a base install. These need something more, and the palette marks each one that this server does not yet have with a "Needs ..." badge ("Needs a real LLM", "Needs an object store", "Needs an MCP server", "Needs an allowlist", "Needs the run queue"). The full sentence is on hover and in the component reference. While CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS is off (the default), an MCP node is reported as unavailable ("A registered MCP server that CALIBER can reach (needs CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true)"). Once it is on, the MCP badge always shows, because a registered MCP server is data that configuration cannot check.

NodeNeedsIf it is missing
agenta real LLM providerthe default fake provider echoes a canned reply, and a calibration of the workflow is marked "Simulated evaluation"
input_bucket, output_bucketa remote object store (MinIO or S3)the bucket cannot be read or written
knowledge_query, knowledge_builda remote object store, and for a query a built knowledge base versionthe node fails at run time
mcp_resourceCALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true (off by default) and a registered MCP server that CALIBER can reachthe node is unavailable ("A registered MCP server that CALIBER can reach (needs CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true)") until the flag is on, and fails at run time if no server is reachable
external_appCALIBER_EXTERNAL_APP_ENTRYPOINT_ALLOWLIST naming the entrypointevery entrypoint is refused until the allowlist is set
human_approval, wait_until, wait_for_eventthe run queue and checkpointing (CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_QUEUE_ENABLED=true and CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_CHECKPOINTING_ENABLED=true)the run cannot pause; see Waits, approvals and queued runs

"Configured" in the palette means the setting is present, not that the service answers; /readiness is what probes reachability.

Preview refuses a workflow that contains any of the file, folder, bucket, mcp_resource, python_code, external_app, webhook or api_request nodes, because it cannot isolate them from the host (a file input pinned to a managed file is the one exception). A python_code node is authorable by operators. Preview refuses it and a published run blocks import, but that is containment, not isolation, and it carries the same trust as a registered tool: the author is trusted. See Who is trusted to write tools.

How a workflow calibration is scored#

Calibrating a workflow replays the baseline and each candidate through the executor and scores them. Under the default fake LLM the executor replays canned outputs, so the run is marked Simulated evaluation (eval_results.simulated is true, and eval_results.provider names the provider). Unless the LLM judge is enabled and available the score is structural (eval_results.scorer is structural, otherwise llm_judge): it checks that the run completed and used its tools, not that the output was good. The workflow's calibration runs show these as a Simulated evaluation badge and a Structural score badge. Read both markers before you apply a candidate.

Who can do what#

Inside a project, creating or changing a workflow or a workflow version, and clearing a workflow's session memory, need editor or owner. Publishing a version, moving an alias and publishing a workflow as a service need editor or owner. Running a workflow, starting a calibration and uploading a file into a run need reviewer, editor or owner. Approving a run that is waiting for approval needs reviewer or owner. Applying a calibration candidate needs editor or owner. A member whose role is too weak gets 403 and a person outside the project gets 404. See Auth and project scoping.

Run with approved runtime lineage#

In the reference profile, the console Run and event Trigger controls require runtime lineage. Open the Run or Deployments surface and select an approved workspace release together with the environment whose current-release pointer matches that release. The console submits both IDs to the existing run or trigger endpoint; it never chooses an organization, bypasses project scope, or overrides server admission.

Only active environments with an exact approved current release are shown. If the project has no such pair, the controls remain disabled and show the stable lineage_required refusal. Create or approve a workspace release and make it current for an active environment, then refresh the page. A release becoming stale between selection and submission is still rejected by the server; keep the selected pair and retry after the environment is current again.

1. What workflows are for in CALIBER#

Workflows are the orchestration surface for multi-step automation. They connect prompts, tools, skills, MCP access, files, and approvals into a governed run model.
